documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25F joining the practice, teaches high school math. Came straight from school.

HPI: Feels well. Hypothyroid since 2018 (antibody positive per old records), on levothyroxine 75 mcg each morning, takes it before coffee, rarely misses. No palpitations, weight stable, energy fine now that the school year is ending.

PMH: hypothyroidism. PSH: none. Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. Allergies: none known.
FH: dad has type 1 diabetes, mom hypothyroid, sister has celiac.
SH: married, no kids yet. Never smoked. Wine on some weekends, a glass or two. No drugs. Runs a couple of times a week.
Gyn: regular cycles. Pap 2020 normal at prior office. HPV series done as a teen.
Imm: COVID x2 this spring.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Well appearing. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin normal. No edema.
PHQ-9: 2.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism, autoimmune: continue 75 mcg. TSH today.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids; one-time HIV and hep C screens discussed and drawn. Pap due 2023. Flu shot in the fall.
3. Given the family history of type 1 diabetes and celiac, reviewed symptoms worth calling about (thirst, urinating a lot, weight loss).

RTC 9 months for a physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning asking to be seen.

S: About 3 weeks of being thirsty all the time, getting up twice a night to pee, and keeping a water bottle on her desk she refills between classes. Pants looser; down about 4 kg from March on our scale. Appetite normal to increased. Some blurry vision at the end of the day. No nausea, vomiting, belly pain or shortness of breath. No fevers. Thyroid pill taken daily.
Father was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes as an adult, so she recognized the pattern.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 59.4 kg. Looks well, not ill or dry. Breathing comfortable, no fruity odor. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Urine dip in office: glucose positive, ketones negative, protein negative.

A/P: new hyperglycemia in a lean 25-year-old with weight loss and a strong autoimmune family history. Type 1 (autoimmune) diabetes is most likely.
- BMP and A1c sent stat.
- Called endocrinology directly; they will see her Friday 5/13.
- Reviewed when to go to the ED: vomiting, abdominal pain, fast breathing, confusion.
- Plenty of water, avoid sugary drinks.

Addendum 18:55: glucose 287, bicarbonate normal, A1c 10.4%. Called her with results. She is feeling the same, no vomiting. Plan unchanged, keep Friday appointment.

documents.title: Nurse check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt on her lunch break per PCP. Still thirsty, no vomiting, eating and drinking fine. Confirmed endocrinology Friday 5/13 at 9:00, she has a sub arranged for her morning classes. Faxed yesterday's labs and visit note to endocrinology. ED precautions repeated, she verbalized them back.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, consultation of 05/13/2022, received by fax.

Reason for referral: new hyperglycemia (glucose 287 mg/dL, HbA1c 10.4%), referred by her primary care physician.

Ms. Pereira is a 25-year-old teacher with three weeks of polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss. Her father has type 1 diabetes; she has autoimmune hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg. No ketosis on her office urine.

Exam: lean build. No acanthosis. Thyroid normal. No signs of dehydration.

Labs drawn here: GAD65 antibody 48 U/mL (reference <5), positive. C-peptide 0.4 ng/mL with a simultaneous glucose of 241 mg/dL. Tissue transglutaminase IgA negative (screened given her sister's celiac disease).

Impression: type 1 diabetes mellitus, new onset, autoimmune.

Plan:
1. Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneously at bedtime.
2. Insulin lispro with meals, 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate. Carbohydrate counting session with our diabetes educator completed today.
3. Fingerstick glucose before meals and at bedtime; log reviewed by phone weekly for now.
4. Hypoglycemia recognition and treatment taught.
5. Return in 3 months; A1c through your office is fine.
6. Annual dilated eye exam recommended.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medications on our list: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, insulin glargine, insulin lispro.

Thank you for this referral.
Endocrinology

One mild low before lunch after a fire drill made her late to eat; treated with juice, felt fine. Learning to count carbs, using an app. Emotionally "a lot to absorb", but her dad has been a good coach. Keeping glucose tabs in her desk.

O: Weight 60.6 kg, up from 59.4. BP and HR as charted. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal, pulses 2+.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes, new: per endocrinology. Weekly log calls with their educator. Will draw A1c in August before her endo follow-up.
2. Vaccines indicated with diabetes: PCV20 and hepatitis B (first of three) given today.
3. Referral for a dilated eye exam this summer.
4. Hypothyroidism: levothyroxine 75 mcg, stable.
5. Letter for school nurse to allow snacks/glucose checks in class: done.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: hospital obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 08/23/2024, discharged 08/25/2024.

Patient: 28-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks 1 day.
Presentation: contractions about every 5 minutes for six hours; membranes ruptured spontaneously two hours before she arrived. Prenatal course uncomplicated and prenatal labs unremarkable.
History: type 1 diabetes; autoimmune hypothyroidism. No surgeries. Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: insulin glargine 22 units subcut at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals at 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; levothyroxine 75 mcg by mouth daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Social: never smoker; no alcohol in pregnancy. Teaches mathematics.

Admission findings: BP 120/78, HR 88, temperature 37.2 C (99.0 F). Fetal heart rate tracing reassuring. Sterile speculum exam: clear fluid. Cervix 6 cm, 90% effaced, vertex at -1 station. Recheck four hours later: 7 cm, 100% effaced.
Labor progressed and she had a normal spontaneous vaginal delivery of a healthy liveborn infant. Insulin per the inpatient protocol during labor, with endocrinology input; home doses resumed after delivery.

Postpartum course uncomplicated. Breastfeeding. Discharged home postpartum day 2.

Diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered; normal spontaneous vaginal delivery; type 1 diabetes; hypothyroidism.
Discharge medications: as above.
Follow-up: obstetrics 6 weeks; endocrinology 2-3 weeks; primary care as scheduled.

Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 08/30/2025, discharged 09/01/2025.

29-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks 1 day in active labor, a year after her first vaginal delivery. Type 1 diabetes and autoimmune hypothyroidism. Glucose was difficult to control throughout this pregnancy, with frequent hyperglycemia and frequent hypoglycemia, despite consistent insulin use and full attendance at prenatal care. Prenatal course otherwise unremarkable.
Allergies: NKDA. Surgical history: none.
Home medications: insulin glargine 22 units subcut at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals, 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; levothyroxine 75 mcg by mouth daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.

On arrival: uncomfortable with contractions, in moderate distress during them. Vital signs stable. Fetal tracing reassuring. Cervix 6 cm, 90% effaced.
Course: delivered by normal spontaneous vaginal delivery two hours after admission. Male infant, 4,500 g (macrosomic). Apgar 8 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes.
Newborn: jittery and irritable at 30 minutes of life. Infant glucose 25 mg/dL; infant hemoglobin 17 g/dL; calcium 9.2 mg/dL; magnesium 2.1 mg/dL; CBC otherwise unremarkable. Neonatal hypoglycemia, managed by the newborn team.
Mother: postpartum course uncomplicated; insulin back to home doses with endocrinology input.

Diagnoses (maternal): term pregnancy, delivered; normal spontaneous vaginal delivery; type 1 diabetes with poor control during pregnancy; hypothyroidism.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home.
Follow-up: obstetrics 6 weeks, endocrinology 1-2 weeks, primary care.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: hospital obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 07/24/2026, discharged 07/27/2026.

30-year-old G3P2 at 38 weeks 4 days with type 1 diabetes and autoimmune hypothyroidism, admitted in labor. Prior vaginal deliveries in August 2024 and August 2025; the 2025 pregnancy had difficult glucose control and the infant had neonatal hypoglycemia.
Allergies: NKDA. Surgical history before this admission: none.
Home medications: insulin glargine 22 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals at 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.

Course: membranes ruptured spontaneously shortly after admission with a large amount of clear fluid. About 15 minutes later she felt something suddenly between her legs, became very anxious and noticed less fetal movement. Nursing noted the fetal heart rate, normal until then, fall to 70 beats per minute and stay there for more than a minute despite position changes and oxygen. Cervix 7 cm; a firm, pulsating cord felt alongside the presenting part, with the head high and poorly applied to the cervix.
Diagnosis: umbilical cord prolapse.
Emergency low transverse cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. Liveborn girl, Apgar 6 at 1 minute and 8 at 5 minutes, admitted to the NICU for observation.
Postoperative course uncomplicated. Insulin per inpatient protocol, back to home doses with endocrinology. Discharged postoperative day 3.

Diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered; umbilical cord prolapse; emergency cesarean delivery; type 1 diabetes; hypothyroidism.
Discharge medications: home medications as above.
Follow-up: obstetrics wound check 1-2 weeks; endocrinology 1-2 weeks; primary care.

documents.title: Baby update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know she came by emergency C-section on the 24th, it was terrifying but we're both ok. She's home with us now. Incision healing, OB checked it last week. Sugars bouncing a bit, endo is on it. I'll set up a postpartum visit once I can drive.

documents.title: Re: Baby update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm so glad you're both okay. I read the hospital summary; that sounds frightening. Message whenever you're ready and we'll find a time. If you notice any mood changes, pain or redness at the incision, or leg swelling, reach out right away.
